title: Doenjang-Butter Grilled Scallops
shortDescription: Dry-packed sea scallops grilled for a browned crust and finished with a savory doenjang-butter glaze balanced with honey, vinegar, garlic, and sesame.
culturalContext: Doenjang is a foundational Korean fermented soybean paste, while butter-based seafood glazes are a modern pairing. This recipe is explicitly contemporary and does not claim that doenjang-butter scallops are a codified traditional dish.

marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: No marination; hold divided glaze in two labeled clean bowls
marinadeOrSeasoning.refrigeratedMarinationTimeRange: No marination; keep scallops and glaze refrigerated separately until preheating begins
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not marinate scallops in the salty glaze; surface moisture prevents browning and salt can draw out water.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Divide the glaze into separate cooking and finishing bowls before raw seafood handling.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard any cooking glaze or brush contaminated by raw or undercooked scallops; finish only with the untouched clean portion.
substitutions: A verified dairy-free solid cooking fat would create a different, separately reviewed recipe and cannot guarantee allergen safety.
White miso is not an equivalent cultural substitute for doenjang; if used, relabel the adaptation and rebalance salt after testing.
allergenNotes: Contains shellfish, soy, dairy, and sesame.
Commercial doenjang may contain wheat; verify its label.

instructions.heading: Select, thaw, and trim
instructions.action: Thaw frozen scallops overnight in the refrigerator. Remove the small firm side muscle if present. Do not rinse.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Scallops smell mild and sweet, feel firm, and are not sitting in milky liquid.
instructions.safetyNote: Reject scallops with sour, strongly fishy, or ammonia-like odor; sanitize the prep area after raw seafood.

instructions.heading: Dry the surfaces thoroughly
instructions.action: Blot scallops on all sides with disposable towels, then coat lightly with neutral oil and black pepper.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Surfaces feel tacky-dry rather than wet and leave no puddle on the plate.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard towels immediately and wash hands after handling raw scallops.

instructions.heading: Mix and divide the glaze
instructions.action: Mash butter and doenjang smooth; mix in honey, vinegar, garlic, sesame oil, and scallion. Divide into separate cooking and finishing bowls with separate brushes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Glaze is uniform, soft, and brushable with no lumps of plain butter.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the finishing bowl and brush outside the raw-seafood zone.

instructions.heading: Preheat for release
instructions.action: Preheat the approved grill or plancha to medium-high, clean thoroughly, and oil lightly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Scallops sizzle on contact and remain stationary without flooding the surface.
instructions.safetyNote: Use only approved indoor electric equipment indoors; follow ventilation, clearance, and grease instructions.

instructions.heading: Sear and turn once
instructions.action: Place scallops with space between them and cook without moving for 2 to 3 minutes. Turn with a clean thin spatula when they release, brush the cooked side with the cooking glaze, and cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
instructions.temperature: Official cue: milky white or opaque and firm
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: First side is browned; center changes from translucent to opaque and the scallop feels firm with slight spring.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not force stuck scallops; inspect the thickest center and discard the cooking glaze and brush after use.

instructions.heading: Finish from the clean bowl
instructions.action: Transfer opaque scallops to the clean platter and apply a very thin layer of untouched finishing glaze.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Scallops are browned, opaque, and lightly glossy without a pool of melted butter.
instructions.safetyNote: Never combine cooking and finishing glaze or reuse raw-contact tools.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high. Follow the appliance manual for ventilation, clearances, grease handling, and grate care; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: FoodSafety.gov lists no numeric minimum for scallops; cook until flesh is milky white or opaque and firm.
visualDonenessCues: The center is milky white or opaque with no translucent raw band.
Scallops are firm with slight spring and have a browned first side.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep seafood at 40°F / 4°C or below and thaw in the refrigerator, not on the counter.
Do not rinse raw seafood; splashing can spread contamination. Peel, devein, or remove side muscles with clean tools, then pat dry.
Use separate raw and cooked plates, tongs, brushes, and skewers, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
FoodSafety.gov directs cooking shrimp and scallops until the flesh is pearly or white and opaque; time alone is not a doneness test.
Pregnant, immunocompromised, older, and very young diners should not be served raw or undercooked seafood.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Wet-packed scallops can be used only after thorough drying, but added solution may inhibit browning; dry-packed is preferred.
Replacing butter or doenjang changes the recipe and requires separate allergen, salt, and cultural review.
ingredientSourcing: Choose dry-packed scallops that are firm, moist but not milky, and mild-smelling.
Frozen packages should be intact without large ice crystals or signs of thawing and refreezing.
Read doenjang labels for soy, wheat, fish, and other possible ingredients because formulations vary.
makeAhead: Mix and divide the glaze up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate. Bring it only to a brushable consistency while the grill preheats. Dry and season scallops immediately before cooking.
storage: Refrigerate cooked scallops within 2 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 2 days. Discard used cooking glaze and individual serving portions.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C using brief gentle heat; scallops toughen quickly, so reheat only once.
leftovers: Slice reheated scallops over rice with fresh greens; do not reuse leftover table glaze unless it remained uncontaminated and continuously refrigerated.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice and crisp fresh vegetables that offset the rich butter glaze.
Use a small amount of glaze so doenjang supports rather than masks the scallops.

faq.question: Why use dry-packed scallops?
faq.answer: They generally release less added liquid, making a browned crust easier. Regardless of type, blot scallops thoroughly and verify freshness.

faq.question: What is the official doneness cue?
faq.answer: FoodSafety.gov instructs cooking scallops until the flesh is milky white or opaque and firm; check the thickest center.

buyingCues: Firm scallops with a mild, sweet sea smell and no sour, strongly fishy, or ammonia-like odor.
Dry-packed scallops are preferred; frozen packaging is intact without large ice crystals or freezer burn.
seafoodPreparation.thawing: Thaw in a covered container overnight in the refrigerator. If using sealed cold-water thawing, cook immediately afterward.
seafoodPreparation.cleaningOrShellPreparation: Remove the small tough side muscle when present. Do not rinse raw scallops.
seafoodPreparation.drying: Blot every side thoroughly with disposable towels immediately before oiling.
seafoodPreparation.grillSurfacePreparation: Use a thoroughly preheated, cleaned, lightly oiled grate or plancha with a thin spatula ready.
seafoodPreparation.stickingPrevention: Choose dry-packed scallops, dry aggressively, oil lightly, leave space, and do not move until a crust forms and releases.
seafoodPreparation.approximateTime: About 4 to 6 minutes total for large sea scallops, depending on thickness and surface heat.
donenessCues: Milky white or opaque through the thickest center.
Firm with slight spring; no translucent raw band remains.
seafoodPreparation.applicableTemperature: FoodSafety.gov provides the visual standard milky white or opaque and firm rather than a numeric scallop minimum.
seafoodPreparation.shellOpeningAndDiscardGuidance: For shucked sea scallops no shell-opening cue applies; reject damaged packaging or scallops with spoilage odors.
crossContactNotes: Use separate cooking and finishing glaze bowls and brushes.
Keep raw scallop plate and utensils away from the clean serving platter and ready-to-eat foods.
